title: At the restaurant: quisiera…
summary: Get a table, order the menú del día course by course, say what you love and what you are allergic to, and ask for the bill.
focus: Ordering food and drink politely and handling a meal out
content:
## A table and the menu

Walking in:

- *Una mesa para dos, por favor.* (A table for two, please.)
- *¿Tienen mesa para cuatro?* (Do you have a table for four?)
- *¿Me trae la carta, por favor?* (Could you bring me the menu?)

Careful, **la carta** is the menu you read; **el menú del día** is the fixed-price lunch most restaurants in Spain serve on weekdays: a starter, a main, dessert or coffee, bread and a drink, usually for 12 to 16 euros.

The waiter (**el camarero**, **la camarera**) will ask *¿Qué van a tomar?* (What will you have?) or *¿Qué les pongo?* **Tomar**, not *comer* or *beber*, is the verb for having food or drink.

## Ordering: de primero, de segundo

A Spanish meal is ordered course by course:

| phrase | meaning |
|---|---|
| **de primero** | for the first course, as a starter |
| **de segundo** | for the main course |
| **de postre** | for dessert |
| **para beber** | to drink |

*De primero, gazpacho; de segundo, pollo asado, y para beber, agua.*

Three ways to ask, from most to least formal:

- **Quisiera** la merluza. (I would like the hake; very polite.)
- **Quería** una ensalada. (I'd like a salad; the everyday choice.)
- **¿Me pone** una caña? (Can I have a small beer? Used at a bar; from **poner**.)

For meat the waiter may ask *¿Cómo lo quiere?*: **poco hecho** (rare), **al punto** (medium) or **muy hecho** (well done).

## Quantities, likes and allergies

Quantities link to the food with **de**, which never changes:

- **un vaso de** agua (a glass of water)
- **una copa de** vino (a glass of wine)
- **una botella de** agua (a bottle of water)
- **una ración de** patatas bravas (a portion of patatas bravas; **media ración** is a half portion)
- **un poco de** pan (a little bread, some bread)

To say you love a dish, use **encantar**, which works like **gustar**: *Me encanta el gazpacho. Me encantan las tapas.*

Allergies use **ser alérgico / alérgica a**: *Soy alérgica al marisco* (shellfish), *a los frutos secos* (nuts), *al gluten*. To check a dish: *¿Lleva cebolla?* (Does it have onion in it?) *Sin cebolla, por favor.*

## Paying and manners

When you finish, catch the waiter's eye and ask:

- *La cuenta, por favor.* (The bill, please.)
- *¿Me cobra?* (Can I pay? Literally, will you charge me?)
- *¿Pagamos juntos o por separado?* (Are we paying together or separately?)
- *¿Se puede pagar con tarjeta?* (Can we pay by card?)

**La propina** (the tip) is not obligatory in Spain and nobody expects 15 %: people round up or leave a euro or two in the little dish. **Invito yo** means *it's on me*.

Two phrases you will hear all the time: **¡Que aproveche!** (enjoy your meal) when the food arrives, and **está buenísimo** (it's delicious) from happy diners.

vocabulary.example_meaning: For the main course I want the grilled fish.

quiz.prompt: ___, un gazpacho; de segundo, el pollo asado.
quiz.explanation: Gazpacho is a starter, so it comes 'de primero'; the main course follows 'de segundo'.
hints: What comes before the second course?

quiz.prompt: ¿Y ___ beber? — Un vaso de vino tinto.
quiz.explanation: Drinks are asked for with 'para beber' (to drink), not 'de': '¿Y para beber?'

quiz.prompt: Choose the most polite way to order: '___ el pescado a la plancha, por favor.'
quiz.explanation: 'Quisiera' (I would like) is the most polite form; 'quiero' is correct but blunter, and 'querer' is just the infinitive.
hints: I would like, not I want.
The special polite form of querer.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the course: De ___, una tarta de queso. (dessert)
quiz.explanation: Dessert is 'el postre', so you order it 'de postre': 'De postre, una tarta de queso.'
hints: The sweet course at the end.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence means 'a portion of patatas bravas to share'?
options: Una ración de patatas bravas para compartir.
Un vaso de patatas bravas para compartir.
Una botella de patatas bravas para compartir.
quiz.correct_answer: Una ración de patatas bravas para compartir.
quiz.explanation: A plate of tapas is 'una ración'; 'un vaso' is a glass and 'una botella' a bottle.
hints: Patatas don't come in a glass.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the right form of encantar: Me ___ la ensalada de esta casa.
quiz.explanation: Encantar works like gustar: 'la ensalada' is singular, so 'me encanta'.
hints: Like gustar: me gusta / me gustan.

quiz.prompt: No puedo comer eso: ___ alérgica al marisco.
quiz.explanation: An allergy is a permanent characteristic, so it takes ser: 'soy alérgica al marisco'.
hints: An allergy does not come and go.

quiz.prompt: El ___ del día cuesta doce euros e incluye pan y bebida.
quiz.explanation: The fixed-price lunch is 'el menú del día'. Remember that 'la carta' is the menu you read.

quiz.prompt: Hemos terminado de comer. ¿Qué le dices al camarero?
quiz.explanation: You ask for the bill: 'la cuenta'. 'La carta' is the menu, and 'la propina' is the tip you may leave afterwards, never something you ask for.

listening.meaning: What do you have for dessert?

listening.note: Quantities take de: un vaso de vino.

listening.text: Mi hijo es alérgico a la leche.
listening.meaning: My son is allergic to milk.
listening.note: An allergy takes ser: es alérgico a.

listening.text: Mi mujer siempre deja dos euros de propina al camarero.
listening.meaning: My wife always leaves the waiter a two-euro tip.
listening.note: New word: el camarero = the waiter.

listening.text: Quisiera el menú del día, con pollo de segundo y agua para beber.
listening.meaning: I would like the set menu, with chicken for the main course and water to drink.

guide.tip: Spanish waiters are brisk, not rude. A short 'de primero, ensalada; de segundo, pollo' is exactly what they want to hear.

conversations.title: The menú del día
conversations.scenario: Lucía and a friend sit down for lunch at a small restaurant in Madrid. Andrés, the waiter, comes to take their order.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Good afternoon. What will you have?
lines.note: tomar: to have food or drink

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: Hi. Do you have a set lunch menu?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí: de primero, gazpacho o ensalada mixta; de segundo, pollo asado o merluza a la plancha.
lines.meaning: Yes: for starters, gazpacho or mixed salad; for the main, roast chicken or grilled hake.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Pues de primero, gazpacho, y de segundo, la merluza. ¿Lleva marisco la salsa? Soy alérgica al marisco.
lines.meaning: Then gazpacho to start, and the hake for the main. Does the sauce have shellfish in it? I'm allergic to shellfish.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: No, no lleva. Es solo ajo, aceite y perejil.
lines.meaning: No, it doesn't. It's just garlic, oil and parsley.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Perfecto. Y para mi amigo, ensalada y el pollo.
lines.meaning: Perfect. And for my friend, salad and the chicken.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Un vaso de vino tinto y una botella de agua, por favor. Ah, ¿y me pone un poco más de pan?
lines.meaning: A glass of red wine and a bottle of water, please. Oh, and could you bring me a bit more bread?
lines.note: un vaso de · una botella de · ¿me pone…?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Claro. ¿Y de postre? Hay flan, fruta o tarta de queso.
lines.meaning: Of course. And for dessert? There's flan, fruit or cheesecake.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Me encanta la tarta de queso! Una, por favor. Y la cuenta cuando pueda.
lines.meaning: I love cheesecake! One, please. And the bill when you have a moment.
lines.note: me encanta + singular · 'cuando pueda' = when you can

bites.title: Three courses and a drink
bites.rule: Order in the Spanish order: de primero (starter), de segundo (main), de postre (dessert) and para beber (drink). The menú del día bundles them for one price.
bites.example: De primero, ensalada; de segundo, pollo; y para beber, agua.
bites.example_meaning: Salad to start; chicken for the main; and water to drink.

bites.title: Three polite ways to order
bites.rule: Quisiera… is the most polite, quería… is the everyday one, and at a bar ¿me pone…? means 'could I have…?'.
bites.example_meaning: Could I have a small beer, please?

bites.title: Quantities with de
bites.rule: Un vaso de agua, una copa de vino, una botella de agua, una ración de bravas, un poco de pan. The de never changes.
bites.example: Una ración de patatas bravas para compartir.
bites.example_meaning: A portion of patatas bravas to share.

bites.title: Allergies and the bill
bites.rule: Soy alérgico/a a + the food (al gluten, a los frutos secos). At the end: la cuenta, por favor. The tip is optional: round up or leave a euro.
bites.example: Soy alérgica al marisco. La cuenta, por favor.
bites.example_meaning: I'm allergic to shellfish. The bill, please.

sorts.title: Which course?
sorts.why: Soups and salads start the meal, meat and fish are the main course, sweets are dessert, and drinks are asked for with para beber.

sorts.title: Encanta or encantan?
sorts.why: Encantar works like gustar: the food is the subject, so a plural dish takes encantan.

sorts.title: How much of it?
sorts.why: Drinks come in a vaso, tapas in a ración, and un poco de is 'a little' of something you don't count.

spots.why: The course phrases are fixed: de primero, de segundo, de postre.
Las tapas is plural and is the subject: me encantan.
An allergy is a permanent characteristic: soy alérgico.

spots.sentence: ¿Me trae un poco con pan, por favor?
spots.why: Quantities take de: un poco de pan.
The bill is la cuenta; cuento means 'I count' or 'a story'.
It is el menú del día: de + el = del.
